summary: Turn local hazard and vulnerability findings into monitored resilience actions. Explore practical assessment and planning skills; view the course outline.
lede: Risk reduction and resilience planning helps local government professionals turn hazard and vulnerability findings into practical priorities. For resilience officers, planners, and disaster-risk practitioners, the course covers establishing a baseline with the Disaster Resilience Scorecard for Cities, screening risks with Quick Risk Estimation, assessing exposure and vulnerability, and prioritizing land-use, infrastructure, and service-continuity actions with owners and indicators for follow-up.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for local government professionals who assess hazards, coordinate resilience work, and move local priorities into plans, budgets, and service decisions.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with local planning, public services, disaster-risk management, or resilience responsibilities is recommended. No coding or programming is required.
